content: 1. The study published in the FASEB Journal in 2015 (Volume 29, Meeting Abstracts, Page 342) by Martínez Martínez ÓA focuses on the impact of nutritional supplements and human capital, analyzing the beneficiaries of the Nutrisano and Nutrivida programs under Mexico's Oportunidades initiative. 2. The 2009 study in Revista Gerencia Políticas Salud (Volume 8, Issue 17, Pages 140-154) by Martínez Martínez ÓA examines the role of nutritional supplements in improving health outcomes within the context of Mexico's Oportunidades program. 3. Martorell R's 2020 publication in the Journal of Nutrition (Volume 150, Issue 7, Pages 1676-1677) discusses the contribution of complementary food supplementation to the development of fat-free mass, albeit to a limited extent. 4. Masuda K and Chitundu M's 2019 randomized trial in Zambia, published in PLoS ONE (Volume 14, Issue 2, Article e0211693), investigates the effects of multiple micronutrient supplementation using Spirulina platensis on infant growth, morbidity, and motor development. 5. A follow-up study by Masuda K and Chitundu M in 2019, published in Nutrients (Volume 11, Issue 4, Article 29), highlights the positive association between Spirulina-based micronutrient supplementation during the first 1,000 days and developmental outcomes in children under five years in Zambia. 6. Matilsky DK, Maleta K, Castleman T, and Manary MJ's 2009 study in the Journal of Nutrition (Volume 139, Issue 4, Pages 773-778) demonstrates that supplementary feeding with fortified spreads leads to higher recovery rates in moderately wasted children compared to corn/soy blends. 7. Maust A et al.'s 2015 research in the Journal of Nutrition (Volume 145, Issue 11, Pages 2604-2609) evaluates the successful management of severe and moderate acute malnutrition using an integrated protocol in Sierra Leone. 8. McDonald CM et al.'s 2019 study in the Journal of Nutrition (Volume 149, Issue 6, Pages 1089-1096) reveals that while percent fat mass increases with recovery in young Malian children treated for moderate acute malnutrition, it does not vary significantly with dietary therapy. 9. A 2014 study by McGill University and collaborators examines the cognitive development effects of iodized salt in Ethiopian children. 10. McGill University's 2015 Phase 2 study explores the impact of fortified cheese and yogurt products on vitamin D status in young children. 11. Médecins Sans Frontières' 2012 study assesses the effectiveness of nutritional supplementation in preventing malnutrition among children with infections in Karamoja, Uganda. 12. Meeks Gardner J et al.'s 1995 research in Child Development (Volume 66, Issue 6, Pages 1785-1797) investigates activity and behavioral development in stunted and non-stunted children and their response to nutritional supplementation. 13. Menon P et al.'s 2007 study in the Journal of Nutrition (Volume 137, Issue 4, Pages 1023-1030) demonstrates that micronutrient sprinkles reduce anemia in children aged 9-24 months when delivered through an integrated health and nutrition program in rural Haiti. 14. Miles CW et al.'s 1987 study in Plant Foods for Human Nutrition (Volume 37, Issue 4, Pages 341-359) evaluates the long-term consumption of beef extended with soy protein and its effects on nutrient intakes and serum zinc levels in men, women, and children. 15. Mize CE et al.'s 1995 research in the Journal of Lipid Research (Volume 36, Issue 6, Pages 1178-1187) compares lipoprotein-cholesterol responses in healthy infants fed diets predominant in oleic acid versus linoleic acid, alongside observations in infants fed a human milk-based diet. 16. Moore N et al.'s 2003 double-blind, randomized trial in the British Journal of Nutrition (Volume 90, Issue 3, Pages 581-587) examines the effects of fructo-oligosaccharide-supplemented infant cereal. 17. Morales J et al.'s 2008 study in the Journal of Food Science (Volume 73, Issue 1, Pages S1-S5) evaluates the sensory properties of nutritional supplements enriched with three different forms of iron in a rural Mexican community. 18. Moursi M et al.'s 2003 study in Public Health Nutrition (Volume 6, Issue 3, Pages 249-257) investigates the impact of consuming amylase-containing gruels on the energy intake and growth of Congolese infants. 19. Nane D et al.'s 2019 research protocol in BMC Public Health (Volume 19, Article 1689) explores the use of local ingredient-based supplementary food as an alternative to corn-soya blends for treating moderate acute malnutrition in children aged 6-59 months in Wolaita. 20. Wageningen University's 2011 study examines the potential of amaranth to improve the iron status of children. 21. Wageningen University and collaborators' 2014 assessment investigates zinc intake from enriched water and other dietary sources in Kisumu, Kenya. 22. Washington University School of Medicine's 2015 study evaluates the efficacy of a once-daily calcium and vitamin D fortified food product in improving bone microarchitecture. 23. Washington University School of Medicine's 2011 study compares the effectiveness of three supplementary foods in treating moderate acute malnutrition. 24. Washington University School of Medicine's 2013 evaluation of the Nutributter program assesses its role in preventing undernutrition. 25. Washington University School of Medicine's 2014 pilot study investigates the use of PUFA-optimized RUTF for severe acute malnutrition. 26. The United States Army Research Institute of Environmental Medicine's 2015 study evaluates the efficacy of a calcium and vitamin D fortified food product in improving bone health. 27. Universidad Autónoma de Querétaro's 2003 study evaluates strategies to treat anemia in Mexican children. 28. The University of Guelph's 2016 study examines the role of ω-3 LCPUFAs in the healthy growth and development of infants and young children in Southwest Ethiopia. 29. The University of Oslo's 2009 study evaluates the effectiveness of supplementary feeding during infection among moderately malnourished children. 30. The University of California Davis's 2017 study assesses the acceptability and tolerance of a protein and micronutrient fortified food. 31. The University of British Columbia's 2015 study evaluates the use of thiamin-fortified fish sauce to combat infantile beriberi in rural Cambodia. 32. The International Centre for Diarrhoeal Disease Research's 2020 study investigates zinc absorption from biofortified rice in Bangladeshi children. 33. The International Centre for Diarrhoeal Disease Research's 2017 study evaluates the impact of vitamin D supplementation on severe pneumonia among children under five.
